strongest_value_story: ECDC short-term forecasting is best defended as CAPACITY SUBSTITUTION: a reliable supranational public good that most member states cannot produce for themselves. The two datasets interlock cleanly. Demand side: 68% of responding NFPs (13/19) report zero in-house mathematical-modelling staff, and free-text confirms real gaps (Luxembourg "no resources," Ireland "limited capacity," Italy outsources to Fondazione Bruno Kessler). Supply side: the RespiCast hubs delivered exactly what those NFPs lack - a multi-model, ensemble-backed forecast every week across two full seasons, with an ensemble present in ~98% of rounds (89/91 ILI & ARI, 87/88 COVID), a median of 7-14 models per indicator, and coverage of 15-30 countries. NFPs recognise the value and prioritise the short-term product: 79% (15/19) expect RespiCast to be useful and, when forced to choose, prefer it over the RespiCompass scenario product 5:1 (5 vs 1); free-text explains why ("Respicast more useful as it is short time frame"; scenarios over a 6-month horizon seen as unlikely to drive decisions). The defensible, non-promotional punchline is that the binding constraint is now demand-side, not supply-side: the hub already supplies robust, sustained coverage, yet realised engagement stays modest (RespiCast mean ~2.1/5) and is throttled by awareness, interpretation support and integration mechanisms - "not used due to low awareness and lack of information on how to use/interpret the data." So ECDC forecasting is a working public good for the capacity-poor majority whose value is currently capped by uptake infrastructure, not by model availability - with a secondary benchmarking role for the few high-capacity NFPs.
overclaims: n=19 is ~19 of ~30 EU/EEA NFPs: every respondent moves a percentage ~5 points. Report as counts, attach no confidence intervals or significance, and never generalise from subgroups - the '>10 staff' cell is a SINGLE respondent, so 'high-capacity NFPs find neither useful' is n=1.

Q5 anchor wording is not in the export: treat 0-5 as ordinal awareness/ENGAGEMENT, not usefulness. Do not translate scores into 'X% find RespiCast useful,' and treat the mean of an ordinal scale as a rough summary only (report medians/distributions alongside).

The declining engagement gradient (Guidance 3.89 > COVID hubs ~2.7 > RespiCast 2.11 > RespiCompass 1.35) is confounded by TIME IN MARKET (guidance since 2020, RespiCast since 2023, RespiCompass since 2024). Lower engagement with newer products likely reflects recency, not inferior value - do not present it as a value ranking.

Q8 is prospective/hypothetical ('will be useful'). Multiple respondents say they have not actually used the outputs and 'plan to review next season.' This is aspirational intent, not demonstrated use - avoid 'NFPs use RespiCast to...'

Capacity does NOT show a strong monotonic link to engagement in the data (short-term forecasting engagement is ~flat across staff levels: 2.42/2.25/3). The value story rests on the NEED gap plus stated preference, NOT on capacity-poor NFPs engaging more - do not claim the latter.

Hub numbers count MODEL PRESENCE, not forecast quality, accuracy or calibration. Coverage is not skill and not value: nothing here shows the ensemble beat the baseline or was well-calibrated. Do not imply the forecasts were good.

'Distinct models' (18/17/25 over two seasons) overstates simultaneous breadth given high model turnover; the honest per-week measure is the median (7/8.5/14). Peaks rose (ARI 9->14, ILI 16->20) but season MEANS were flat-to-down (COVID 8.0->7.4, ILI 12.3->11.4), so this is not a clear 'growing participation' story.
Country-coverage counts locations forecast by >=1 model/ensemble, not national UPTAKE. A country appearing in the ILI panel does not mean its NFP uses the output.

NFP awareness is not national engagement: several NFPs note in-house or partner teams already submitting to the hubs (Institut Pasteur, UHasselt/UNamur, Bruno Kessler), so 'NFP not aware' understates country-level involvement.
Response bias: the 19 respondents may be more engaged than the ~11 non-respondents, biasing engagement and value estimates upward. Non-response is unaddressed.
The end-of-series drop to 0-2 models (mid-2026) is summer off-season / incomplete current weeks, not a coverage collapse - use season-level units, not the tail.

'Inform surveillance' being the top intended decision use (58% likely) while healthcare-capacity planning - the canonical forecasting use case - is the LEAST likely (16% likely, 42% unlikely) should be reported as a limitation on decision impact, not buried; value is concentrated in situational awareness, not high-stakes resource decisions.
suggested_analyses: Directly test the capacity->supply link: map each of the 19 NFP countries to whether a team from that country submits to the RespiCast hubs, then cross-tab in-house staff and Q8 value against national hub participation. This turns two separate datasets into one causal-adjacent story instead of parallel anecdotes.

Bring in forecast SKILL to convert 'coverage' into 'value': compute WIS / interval coverage / calibration of the hub ensemble vs the quantileBaseline and vs individual models. This is the single biggest missing piece - stakeholders (r12) explicitly asked for performance metrics, and value claims currently rest on presence alone.

Build an awareness->value funnel (aware -> engaged -> intends to use -> has a clear integration mechanism, Q10) to locate the binding constraint quantitatively; ~half (47%) report a clear integration mechanism, so quantify the drop-off that caps realised value.

Recency-adjust engagement: compare RespiCast against the older COVID Forecast Hub at equivalent maturity (months since launch) to separate 'time in market' from intrinsic value and defuse the recency confound in the engagement gradient.

Per-country coverage depth and reliability: how many countries have >=3 models every week vs sporadic coverage (COVID reaches only 15 countries)? Flag thin-coverage countries as capacity-building / recruitment targets.

Systematic thematic coding of Q8b/Q13 free-text into a small set (benchmarking-vs-decision use; awareness/interpretation barriers; capacity-building/funding asks; short-term-preferred-over-scenario) with counts, to give the qualitative signal defensible weight at n=19.
Non-response characterisation: identify which countries did not respond and whether they skew high or low capacity; at minimum caveat direction of bias, ideally reweight.

Channel-by-audience tailoring: cross Q11/Q12 preferences with capacity - newsletter+website dominate for RespiCast while analysts want meetings for scenarios and 'policy decision-maker meetings' rank last for both - to inform how RespiCompass in particular is packaged and to whom.

Probe the decision-use mismatch: why healthcare-capacity planning (canonical forecast use) is least likely while surveillance is most likely - test whether forecast horizon or geographic granularity limits capacity-planning use, which is actionable for product design.
key_findings: Capacity gap is the dominant fact: 68% of NFPs (13/19) report zero in-house modelling staff; only one reports >10. Free-text corroborates outsourcing and 'no resources' realities.

RespiCast supply is robust and sustained: ensemble present in ~98% of weekly rounds over two seasons (89/91 ILI & ARI; 87/88 COVID); median 7 (ARI), 8.5 (COVID) and 14 (ILI) models per round; country breadth 25 (ARI), 15 (COVID), 30 (ILI).

Short-term forecasting is clearly preferred over scenarios: 79% (15/19) expect RespiCast useful vs 58% for RespiCompass; forced single choice favours RespiCast 5:1; free-text prefers the short horizon and doubts 6-month scenarios drive decisions.

Engagement/awareness is modest and demand-limited, not supply-limited: RespiCast mean 2.11/5 (17% not even aware), RespiCompass 1.35/5 (29% not aware); a respondent attributes non-use to 'low awareness and lack of information on how to use/interpret the data.'

Engagement declines with product recency (Guidance 3.89 > COVID hubs ~2.7 > RespiCast 2.11 > RespiCompass 1.35) - most plausibly a time-in-market effect, and a confound to control, not a clean value ranking.
Value is largely prospective: several NFPs state they have not yet used the outputs and 'plan to review next season,' so Q8 measures expected, not demonstrated, value.

Intended decision use is concentrated in situational awareness: 'inform surveillance' is the top use (58% likely) while healthcare-capacity planning - the classic forecasting use case - is the LEAST likely (16% likely; 42% unlikely).

Two distinct value modes by capacity: capacity-poor NFPs frame ECDC output as substitution/support (11/13 zero-staff NFPs see value in RespiCast/both), whereas the highest-capacity NFP uses it for BENCHMARKING ('we use them to compare our own modelling') and chose 'neither useful.'
Only ~47% (9/19) agree they have a clear mechanism to integrate modelling into decisions (32% disagree) - an integration/infrastructure bottleneck downstream of forecast supply.

Preferred dissemination channels: newsletter/mailing list and website dominate for RespiCast (top-2 74% and 84%); scenario audiences give more weight to analyst meetings; 'online meetings for policy decision-makers' rank last for both products.

Participation breadth is stable, not clearly growing: per-week peaks rose (ARI 9->14, ILI 16->20) but season mean model counts were flat-to-slightly-down (COVID 8.0->7.4; ILI 12.3->11.4; ARI 6.3->7.3).

Explicit capacity-building asks emerge from free-text: an ECDC recommendation and sustainable EU funding for national modelling capacity, training courses, model-performance transparency, and tighter RespiCast-ERVISS linkage.
